items.text: \[Patch Introduction]
New Weapon: Lancaster

A four barreled, medium ammo pistol with a rotating firing pin which allows for a high fire rate. Favored by Hunters on safari as a self-defense weapon due to its superior reliability and stopping power. Opening the break-action will always eject all rounds.
Basic - 4/12
High Velocity - 4/8
Poison - 4/12
Can be dual-wielded.
New Variant: Lancaster Cleaver
A variant of the Lancaster with an under-barrel blade, changing its melee attacks to be similar to a Heavy Knife in both swing pattern and damage.
Basic - 4/12
High Velocity - 4/8
Poison - 4/12
Can be dual-wielded.
World
All Bileweaver Infested Compounds (new and Old) will have a chance to spawn in Chapter 3. There will be 5 compounds active per game.
Fair Play Follow Up
Players get a follow up notification when a player they reported was banned
Players get a Hunt Dollar refund when they get killed by a player who was banned
High ping queue (Temporary test in Europe for the duration of Chapter 3)

Players get matchmade into a separate queue if their ping is above a threshold. The goal is to reduce exposure to high-latency gameplay. Should they not be able to find a match, they rejoin the regular matchmaking queue.
\[Upcoming Updates]
New Community Event: “Reap the Harvest”

“Reap the Harvest” is a new Community Event that is planned to start later in Chapter 3. The Community Event will consist of 5 Stages, each offering a reward to the whole of the community. Players will progress the Community Event by earning Community Event Points which is done by completing objectives in matches.
Community Event Stage Rewards
Stage 1: 5K Hunt Dollars & 1K Event Points
Stage 2: Lancaster (New Weapon)
Stage 3: 10K Hunt Dollars & 2.5K Event Points
Stage 4: Lancaster Cleaver (New Weapon)
Stage 5: Random Legendary Skin

The Inferno Time of Day is back to Hunt, bringing wildfires raging across all maps. It comes with reduced visibility due to heavy smoke and wildfires in affected areas. Wildfires are fixed in location, blocking key traversal paths and forcing new route planning. AI will generally avoid wildfire zones, but if necessary, enemies may follow players through the flames or take shortcuts across them. Inferno will remain part of the active Time of Day Rotation throughout Chapters 2 and 3.
Firefighter Supply
This type of supply only appears during the Inferno Time of Day.
Find valuable rewards such as the Flame Rifle, Scouting Map, or Tarot Cards.
Flame Rifle
Scarce Weapon that releases pressurized liquid producing a steady burst of flames.
They are guaranteed to be found at the Firefighter Supply
The All Hallow’s Cleave Community Event consists of 5 Stages. Players will progress the Community Event by earning Community Event Points which is done by completing objectives in matches.
Stage 1: New Tarot Card: The Atlas
Reveals all hidden locations on the map.
Stage 3: New Tarot Card: The Temperance
Restores the last Trait lost by your hunter this mission.
Dev Note: Using the card also returns traits lost to Siphon, not just burn traits.
Stage 5: New Tool: Long Derringer
A small single-shot pistol that fires Long Ammo, which deals high damage with a reduced velocity and short drop range. More accurate from short to medium range.
The Flame Rifle will come in handy as the Bileweavers are making their comeback in Chapter 2. They have infested 20 new Compounds across all maps, 5 of which will be selected for each match.
We are also introducing their deadlier relatives, the Bloodweavers.
They are Bileweaver variations that cause Bleeding damage with their jump attack and egg-hatching.
Players can identify them by their red-colored body.
The color of Bileweaver Eggs has changed to better reflect their poisonous nature, and Bloodweaver Eggs inherit the red-colored ones with spikes.
They are only present during the Blood Moon Time of Day.
Bileweavers, Bloodweavers, and the infected new Compounds will all arrive with All Hallows’ Cleave on Oct 13th.

Bloodskin is the newest Boss Target: A bloodthirsty being whose protective shell hides the horror that lurks deep within. Those who seek it should beware. The fight begins against a slow, hard-hitting, heavily-armored beast. But once you remove its armor and lower its health, it shifts into a distinct second phase—as an agile abomination with new and bloody abilities. If you defeat Bloodskin, it drops the “Siphon” Trait. When Bloodskin’s banish begins, nearby monsters become more aggressive, like when they are affected by the Blood Moon.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30897473/7271a561b2719d3dd388cbbf3c4645d11a28f46e.png"]

A new and dynamic Time of Day—or rather, time of night—rises over the Incursion areas and shifts between two phases throughout your Mission. During the Intense Blood Moon phase, a storm grows and the moon breaks through the clouds. Monsters become more aggressive and attack faster. During the Dark Blood Moon phase, clouds cover the moon, reducing visibility and returning monster behavior to normal. Both phases bathe the map in a red glow, with the effect becoming stronger and brighter when the Blood Moon leaves its cloud cover.
New weapon: Burgess

The Burgess is a foldable, slide-action, long barrel shotgun with a Weapon Capacity of Size 3 at the cost of a long equip and unequip animation. It features a 6-round magazine. It can be equipped with the “Bulletgrubber” Trait to recover ejected live shells.

Hidden Information Changes
All Supply Points, Scout Towers, and Extraction Points are hidden by default.
Investigating a Clue will now reveal 2 Extraction Points.
The Scouting Maps that reveal hidden info can now appear at all Supply Points.
Scout Towers still have a guaranteed Scouting Map inside.
The Spyglass still reveals hidden location icons on the compass.
The radius to discover hidden locations has been increased to 75m.

Dev Note: We’ve taken note of community feedback and hope this alleviates some of the pain points of the previous iterations of the hidden info mechanic. We hope this adds focus to the core game loop, while adding the element off discovery by keeping a lot of information hidden.
Trait Changes

New Burn Trait: Siphon - Allows you to loot a Scarce Trait off an enemy Hunter’s body, leaving Siphon in its place. Siphon can be acquired by interacting with Blood Wells or found in-world like other Scarce Traits. Siphon will also be dropped by Bloodskin.

Dev Note: Siphon will prioritize Death Cheat whenever possible, and if not, it will steal a random Scarce Trait if the looted Hunter had one. For solos, if not Death Cheat, it will then prioritize Necromancer, but you will not be able to steal Necromancer from another solo player, only from someone in a team. When Death Cheat is stolen, it will still be active for the player that lost it for the rest of the round.
New Burn Trait: Chupacabra - Interact with a live horse, cow, or animal cage to restore 1 Health Chunk.

Dev Note: Once unlocked, Chupacabra will be buyable from the Trait menu for 2 Upgrade Points. When interacting with dog cages, all 3 dogs can be interacted with separately, while for chickens the entire cage can be interacted with once. The chosen animal is triggered during the interaction and killed upon completion.
Vulture: Now gets a Catalyst Conditional which allows players to loot some ammo from downed Hunters.
Lightfoot: Now gets the Catalyst Conditional to never break branches. This effect was previously part of the Catalyst Conditionals for Beastface, but has now been moved to Lightfoot.
Added Crackshot, Blademancer, and Corpse Seer to the list of possible Trait spawns at Scout Towers and themed Supply Points. Both Sealed and normal Trait Spur variations can spawn.
Destiny’s Dial now has a chance to reveal all hidden locations as a reward.
Postal Supply now only contains the Experience Boon, with the other Boons moving to more thematically appropriate Supply Points.
Clockmaker’s Supply now contains a Dark Sight Boon.
Reduced the chance of Sealed Boons to spawn in Scout Towers and Supply Points.

notes.title: o Agitated monsters have the following Traits

items.text: § A dark, smoky aura.
§ They sound more aggressive.
§ They have slightly sharper senses while roaming.
§ They move faster. Armoreds and Leeches are most affected by the change, while Hellhounds and Immolators retain their original movement speed.
§ Grunts, Armoreds, and Firebreathers (when wet) attacks occur at shorter intervals, so they deal more damage over time.
§ Attack animations for Grunts, Armoreds, Firebreathers (when wet), Brutes, Ursa Mortises, and Meatheads are faster.

· Immolator navigation has been nerfed, no longer allowing the monster to figure out long, complex paths to players. Detection distances remain the same, preserving the experience in open fields where the Immolator has a straight path to its target.
· Hellhounds are now slower when they are in water or have a mutilated leg.
2 Stages: Bloodskin transforms mid-encounter, changing the dynamics of the fight. It never returns to Stage 1 after transforming.
Stage 1: Slow, armored creature. Dangerous in close-quarter combat, he hits hard.
Stage 2: Fleshy, agile being who teleports around to ambush the player.
Drops the “Siphon” Trait when he dies.
When banish begins, nearby monsters become more aggressive, like when they are affected by the Intense Blood Moon phase of the “Blood Moon” Time of Day. Effects last for the duration of the banish.
Low visibility Time of Day rates have been reduced for new players to ease their first steps in the game.
Bloodskin (new Boss Target) is excluded from new-players-only Missions (all players below Bloodline Rank 11).
Traits in Loadouts
A much-requested feature is finally here! You are now able to add Traits to Custom Loadouts and, in the process, hopefully cut down on the number of steps to re-equip a Hunter after death.
Custom Loadouts now come with a dual cost: Hunt Dollars and Upgrade Points.
You can equip 0-15 Traits to a loadout. Cost is replaced with total budget needed.
The cost of the Traits will be applied when you equip the Loadout to your Hunter.
If you have insufficient Upgrade Points, you will not be allowed to equip the Loadout and will be shown an error message.
You can still copy your Hunter's loadout into a Custom Loadout slot.
Scarce and Locked Traits cannot be copied over to a Custom Loadout from a Hunter. Those items will be skipped once the action is taken.
You can disable the Traits widget if you want to equip the Custom Loadout without the Traits.
Hunter Slots
Expanded the total possible number of Hunter Slots from 75 to 100.
Made improvements to the localization for French, Russian, Chinese Simplified, and German.
MMR Decay
Returning players will now receive a temporary MMR modifier that slightly reduces difficulty of Missions after a longer break from the game.
This modifier gradually decreases the more you play, perfect for when you are feeling rusty and need a few games to get back on track.
New Player Modifier
Before, this was a flat-value MMR reduction that was turned off at specific Bloodline Rank, resulting in a spike of difficulty for new players.
Now it uses similar logic to MMR Decay—a modifier that smoothly increases difficulty and gives newcomers a fair fighting chance against more experienced (but similarly skilled MMR-wise) players.

notes.title: Player Profile Customization - DLC Hunter Avatars

items.text: Have you been customizing your Player Profile Cards? If so, we have good news for you: With Chapter 2 of Road to Hell, we are adding several Avatars from some much-loved DLC. This means if you own one of the DLC listed below, then you will automatically receive the corresponding Avatar with this release.

We are working on having an Avatar available for every Legendary Hunter from our collection of DLC. The team have been working hard on making some of your favorites, and we wanted to launch these as soon as we had a batch ready so you weren’t left waiting. Hunters,

The launch of Road to Hell is off to a great start! Our concurrent player numbers have climbed into the top three in Hunt's history, and it's been fantastic to see so many of you jumping into the action and exploring the new update.
With that, we wanted to take a moment to address some of the feedback we have seen online.

We have seen plenty of lively discussions around balancing and the new metas forming in 2.8. We love it. It's exactly this kind of passion that makes the community what it is, and we want to reassure you that all of it is being read and digested by the team. Your opinions are being carefully considered, and we will be keeping a close eye on the conversation going forward as these new meta starts to settle. Keep it coming!

A few of you have raised concerns that the new Points of Interest (Stronghold, Medical Supply, and Military Supply) can on rare occasions spawn too close together. Their placement is intentional and strategic, designed to drive higher engagement, but we understand the feedback. Some of the rules that drive our placement logic will also shift when the second possible Stronghold locations arrive in Chapter 2. We will be monitoring spawn locations and their impact on gameplay closely as well over the next few days before making any decisions on potential changes.

We couldn't help but notice some frustration around the removal of Dumdum and other Custom Ammo, along with the changes that come with it. We recognize this will cause a meta shift and have taken this step in response to player feedback on how these ammo types were driving a stale meta. We are genuinely excited to see what fresh loadouts the community will build in response, and we are weighing all of your opinions and match data for future development. This change creates a clean slate and a return to core Hunt gameplay, from which we can further build and tune while staying true to the spirit of the more tactical gunplay that makes us different from all the other shooters. Reminder that we’ve increased the Loadout limit from 15 to 30 with this update, so you have more room for experimentation.

Lastly, some of you have mentioned that Supply Crates aren't quite what you expected. Without giving too much away, we have an exciting twist on how Supply Crates will be used in the game arriving with Chapter 2 in July—a small teaser of which is hidden on our roadmap graphic. Stay tuned!
Thank you so much for your passion, feedback, and attention to detail.
Happy Hunting, Hunters.
Update 2.8 - The Road to Hell Starts Now

When two military scouts go missing while investigating the Corruption in Louisiana and Colorado, their concerned Commander decides to go after them. But his request for an official mission is declined, and instead he goes rogue and forms The 26th Regiment. With the financial backing of Desolation’s Delegate, the 26th are indignant at the lack of official support, but certain they can find their comrades and clean up the alleged Corruption themselves. They are professionals: well-trained and well-armed.

Their first mistake is their arrogance. Their second is their optimism. The Corruption is like nothing they have encountered before. Beset by monsters on one side and enemy Hunters who don’t want outside involvement on the other, their arrogance is transformed into doubt and then twisted into madness as they all lose themselves to the Hunt.

The Stronghold is where The 26th Regiment had their last stand. Few survived the experience, and many who didn’t now wander the area, Corrupted and transformed into mindless Grunts. Here you won’t just find Destiny's Dial, Sealed Rewards, and Tarot Cards—but some new and interesting secrets…
The Strongholds are large and have 3 main areas to them: the trenches, the camp, and the fortified building. The camp area has a big mess tent where you will find:

Tarot Cards and more...

With Update 2.8, we want to bring back the scouting mechanics we introduced in 2.7, but with some changes to address the community's feedback.

Scout Towers have been removed for Update 2.8. Instead, at the start of the Mission, the Stronghold, Medical Supply, and Military Supply will all be visible at the start of the Mission. Other Supply Points and Extraction Points will be hidden.
These 3 locations all have Scouting Maps. Interacting with Scouting Maps reveals all the hidden locations.
The Scouting Map no longer reveals the location of Wild Targets.
Banishing Targets, picking up a Bounty Token, or using “The Chariot” Tarot Card will still reveal all Extraction Points.

The Maxim M1895 is a new in-world weapon which can only be found at the Stronghold, with each Event Compound containing only one due to limited numbers of the prototype weapons. Previously used as a mounted gun, this version has been ripped off the mount and had some makeshift adjustments, allowing it to be shot from the hip. To accommodate the makeshift portability, ammo bags have been affixed to the sides so that a limited amount of ammo can be carried with the gun.
As an in-world weapon, it cannot be extracted or carried in a Hunter's inventory. Instead, it acts like current Shovels and Lanterns etc. do.
Even if taken to an Extraction Point, it will be left behind.
Due to its makeshift usage, it’s quite cumbersome and will slow Hunters down by 25% when equipped.
Being fired from the hip means that there is a large spread. Aiming will reduce the spread slightly, but is still not accurate.
Due to poor cooling following its prototype nature, it can overheat under extended fire, causing a malfunction which needs to be cleared manually. Best to keep the fire rate low to avoid stoppages!
It has 50 Incendiary rounds by default, but cannot be resupplied.
With Update 2.8, we are launching an inventory rework that aims to open new possibilities, promote loadout diversity at all skill levels, and give more weapons unique, viable niches.
Weapons are assigned a Size from 1 to 5, as opposed to the previous convention of small, medium, and large .
The player's default Weapon Capacity is 5, which can be extended to 6 with the “Quartermaster” Trait.
Tools and Consumables are no longer restricted by type. Players can freely equip any Tool or Consumable to any slot, in any combination.
Consumables are restricted to 4 instances of the same type (Throwables, Deployables, Shots, and Tarot Cards)
Tool Boxes no longer resupply Consumables, instead only resupplying used Tools.

New filter options have been added to the arsenal menu to help sort for the different weapon sizes, Tools, Consumables as well as category filters for Throwables, Deployables, Shots, and Tarot Cards. These have (for now) replaced some of the previous more granular filters for specific damage types for the sake of a better overview.
A lot of secondary balancing went in across the full arsenal to make weapons, Tools, and Consumables fit their new categories. Certain Traits, like Quartermaster, have also been increased in cost.
You can find the full list further below.

Dev note: With this rework, weapons that are equipped on already existing Hunters and would no longer fit due to the slot size changes will be unequipped and placed into your arsenal. This also counts for Contraband items—even if the Contraband limit will be exceeded by this, you will not lose your collected weapons.

Carbine version of the standard military rifle of the US Army until the introduction of the Krag. This lightweight version was mostly used by Cavalry and rear-echelon troops, while still packing the punch of a Long Ammo black powder cartridge. Cheap and readily available, the 1890 model upgrade offers improved sights and handling since it was first introduced in 1873.
Added 1890 Cavalry, a Size 3, single-shot Long Ammo rifle. Compatible with the “Fast Fingers” Trait.
1/18 Ammo Reserve
139 damage
380 m/s muzzle velocity
CATs: FMJ & High Velocity

Dev note: The weapon does not look like much at first glance, but once its role within the wider Inventory Slot Rework is better understood, the advantage of a punchy and cheap single-shot long ammo rifle at Size 3 becomes a lot clearer. The 1890 Cavalry is a great companion weapon for some of the more diverse and affordable loadout choices we want to encourage with this system work. In addition, it is a very good thematic fit for the increased military presence in Road to Hell, where a lot of the service rifles the military brought along would naturally end up in the hands of Hunters.

notes.title: New Free Story Challenge: Let the Gunshots Ring

items.text: With Update 2.8, we are introducing a brand-new and free Story Challenge to the game: Let the Gunshots Ring. Designed with a focus on player onboarding, players follow in the steps of John Victor, a well-seasoned Hunter who is ready to show them the ropes. As they are guided through the story’s Chapters and Challenges, players learn more about and deepen their knowledge of the game’s core gameplay and mechanics all the while earning valuable rewards for free.
“Life is cheap, and sometimes the only way to learn is the hard way.”
John Victor
Chapters: 4
Chapter Rewards: 4

Dev note: Alongside the Inventory Slot Rework, we are taking the opportunity to make significant balance changes to existing weapons to redefine their role and performance in the new weapon economy. Special Long Ammo weapons will continue to be among the best items in the arsenal, but with new constraints requiring adaptation and extra precision.
The following ammo types have been made scarce:
All Dumdum Ammo
All Explosive Ammo (includes Frag Arrows, Explosive Bolts, and Waxed Frag charges)
All Spitzer Ammo
All but 3 instances of the above ammo types have been removed from players’ inventories, and their purchase price refunded.
Dolch FMJ ammo, previously scarce, has now been retired. All instances in players’ inventories have been refunded.

Dev note: With Update 2.8 we are approaching scarcity differently, targeting high-value ammo types by category. As part of this effort, Dolch FMJ stood out as an exception that we wanted to resolve for consistency. We also want the new scarcity to mean more across the board, therefore we decided a reset of the current inventory for all players allows for a clean slate.

releases.displayName: Developer Insight - Fair Play Task Force Update

items.text: We return once again with a long-awaited update from our Fair Play Task Force. We know how important these updates are to the community, and over the last few months our team has been heads down implementing some critical features, and given the sensitive nature of that work, the timing simply wasn't right to speak openly about it until now. But this changes today!

We are pleased to announce that we've partnered with Anybrain — an external solution that collects in-game inputs (mouse, keyboard and controller) and analyzes it to detect abnormal behaviors to figure out who is actively cheating either with hardware or software.

notes.title: We decided to partner with Anybrain for two main reasons

items.text: Detecting mouse-and-keyboard players playing in a controller environment.
This is something that will be enforced as a bannable offence on consoles going forward.
So far, this effort has already resulted in 296 bans on consoles.
Detecting aimbots and scripting on PC.

While we haven't reached the stage of issuing mass sanctions yet, this is a deliberate part of our rollout. We are currently refining our detection criteria on PC to ensure reaching a definitive verdict on bad actors while avoiding false positives.

To get ahead of any questions: Anybrain is not here to replace our team. It's here to empower them with the tools and accuracy that it brings. Our Customer Support team remains fully dedicated to identifying and actioning cheaters, and Anybrain works alongside them and Easy Anti-Cheat (EAC) to strengthen and sharpen that process.

Our detection tools are also fully GDPR-compliant. To put some wild theories to rest: we aren't training predictive social models, monitoring your mood, or harvesting personal data. The system is only focused on one thing: distinguishing between legitimate mouse/keyboard or controller inputs and fake, software-assisted ones.
The end-goal of this partnership is to make Hunt a fairer and more competitive environment for all players.

​Some of you noticed the EULA update wasn't advertised ahead of the release. This was a strategic decision to maximize the impact on cheaters: we opted not to disclose it in advance for the "element of surprise" that prevented cheat users from pausing their software before our system went live. We understand this caused some frustration, and for that, we apologize, but it was a choice made in the best interest of the game's immediate health.
We have also seen a lot of questions about how our detection and ban process works, so here's a transparent look at how it all comes together.

We work alongside Easy Anti-Cheat, which delivers automated ban waves whenever new or updated cheating software is detected, while our own dedicated Customer Support team rigorously reviews every community report and manually determines whether a ban is warranted. This manual step is intentional and very important.

This is what makes our partnership with Anybrain so valuable: combined with EAC, it gives our team sharper, more reliable data to work with, helping us act with both speed and confidence. The goal has always been the same: protect legitimate players and make absolutely sure we are banning the right ones, and not penalising skillful players making incredible shots.

Hunt: Showdown is a commercial product, and we recognize that issuing a ban revokes access to a game you have invested time and resources into. This is a responsibility we take seriously. Our team works to ensure we have a high degree of confidence that a player is in violation of our Terms of Service before any action is taken, balancing the need for a clean competitive environment with the rights of our players.

Since we recognize the potential for false positives in any complex detection ecosystem, we have a dedicated Appeals System in place, accessible through customer support on our website. If you believe a sanction has been applied to your account in error, you can submit a formal request for review. Every appeal triggers a comprehensive manual investigation by our Customer Support team, who will re-examine the data associated with the ban to ensure the correct decision was made.
We have noticed that cheating reports go hand in hand with reports about ping abusers, so we would like to give you an update on this topic as well.

Ping-based limitations are something we are committed to addressing. Right now, we are in the process of tackling substantial technical obstacles in the implementation of this system. The simple truth is, this feature was announced too early, when the very first experiments went live, and we had underestimated the complexity of the topic significantly. The system was not fit for purpose, and that is why it had to go back to the drawing board.
We know how important this feature is to the community, and it remains a priority. We should hopefully have an update for you soon.

Lastly, we are aware that some players have been experiencing increased CPU usage since the launch of update 2.7. Our recently deployed fix has resolved the issue for many, but we know some of you are still affected.
We are continuing to investigate and work on a solution. We hope to have more information to share on this soon.

As always, we appreciate all of your feedback and input on all of the above. We are excited to give you more updates on all of those later in the year, and of course, we hope you are already noticing the impact of our newly implemented features.
Hunters,

Gather your courage, Hunters. It’s time to brave Devil’s Trail.

Experience the bayou and gulch in a whole new way as you're left to track your enemies and scout out points of interest on the map. Keep an eye out for sure signs of enemy Hunters: used bandages, broken barrels, open doors, and more. Use caution as you approach the Scout Towers that will reveal hidden information on your map. Follow the dark plumes of smoke in the sky to find secret rewards. But beware—there's a new monster out to melt the flesh from your bones with its brutal fiery attacks. Think you can handle the heat?
A new fire-breathing monster makes its way to the bayou and gulch. Found amongst groups of Grunts, the Firebreather spews fire from a distance and will require care to dispatch.
The Firebreather has a long-range fire breath, but will stand still before attacking.
Not quite a Grunt, and not quite an Immolator, but shares attributes from both
Small bursts of fire erupt from the body when you pierce its skin with bullets and blades, but it does not fully burst into flames
On death, the Firebreather may let out a final blaze of fire with his last breath, depending on where it got hit.
To bring it down, keep your distance and use ranged weapons, or if you are daring, strike it with a blunt weapon at the right moment and back away.
Temporarily loses its fire breathing attack when exposed to water and hitting it directly with a Water Bottle or Choke cloud will kill it instantly.
Watch out, Firebreathers and explosives don’t mix well.

Dev note: With the Devil’s Trail event, we are aiming to bring a new gameplay dynamic to Bounty Hunt by limiting gameplay information. This is intended to encourage objective play and exploration, giving the advantage to players who engage with boss targets or take the time to locate points of interest before a fight. We’ll closely monitor the community’s feedback on these new event mechanics.
During Devil’s Trail, Supply Points and Extraction Points are hidden from the map.
To reveal the locations of Supply Points and Extraction Points, players can:
Find and interact with a Scouting Map in-game
Discover the locations themselves by walking up to them, pinging them from a distance, or locating them with the Spyglass
Extraction Point locations can additionally be revealed by:
Picking up a Bounty Token
Banishing a Boss Target
Using “The Chariot” Tarot Card.
New tower archetype, which contains special loot and new interactions.
Two Scout Towers appear in every Mission, they will be the only points marked on the map at the start of a match. Players should go there to reveal more of the map.
Scout Towers contain:
A new interactive Scouting Map, which reveals all hidden Supply Points, Extraction Points, Wild Targets and Sealed Bounty Tokens present.
New Tarot Cards to help you track other Hunters
Custom Ammo, Traits, and weapons
When used, the Tarot Card shows the direction to the closest enemy Hunter.
The direction is given via a particle effect in the world and a temporary compass marker. The effect will disappear again after a few seconds.
If no Hunter is present, the Tarot Card will dissipate without spawning an effect.
The Tarot Card can be used at any point in the Mission to either find enemy teams or reveal whether other teams are present at all.

Dev Note: While having some overlap with “The Hanged Man” Tarot Card, “The High Priestess” is more inclined to help track down the closest enemy hunter more easily, while “The Hanged Man” provides more info about the hunter being tracked. “The High Priestess” being a passive ability also leans itself towards being used in combat as it doesn’t take the player out of the fight.
The Tarot Card reveals all used Clues on the map at the time of the card’s usage, with:
Used Clues in red
Highlighting will disappear after some time.
Using the Tarot Card while having another The Pathfinder active updates the map and resets the timer
Dev Note: Timing is key with the “The Pathfinder” and waiting for the right moment will give players the most value out of the card.
World location serving as a new point of interest on the map with unique loot
Players can always find the Catalyst Trait, “The Empress” and “The Chariot” Tarot Cards, A Full Health Restoration Kit and more at the Burned Convoys
Not visible on the map by default—must be located via map interaction or in person
Burned Convoys emit large plumes of smoke, allowing them to be located from a distance
When having the Trait equipped, a player's Dark Sight audio changes drastically
The usual noise accompanying Dark Sight gets toned down, making all audio easier to distinguish while using it
Hunter audio coming from the player’s view direction becomes louder and more pronounced
The Trait can be found at the Scout Towers and Burned Convoys and acquired for 2 Pledge Marks

Increased the damage multiplier for basic Compact Ammo (all non-FMJ) from 0.7 to 0.75 after penetrating 1 layer, and from 0.4 to 0.5 after the second layer.: Dev note: This change effectively should result in compact ammo being able to more reliably penetrate thin surfaces such as fences and wooden planks, especially over distance. With this change, we are aiming to reduce instances of frustrating or confusion instances of no penetration with compact ammo, making it feel more reliable and consistent.
Slightly increased the maximum material thickness all non-FMJ Compact Ammo can penetrate.
Vetterli 71 Cyclone
Decreased damage from 124 to 120
Increased vertical recoil from 6 to 7
Reduced reserve ammo from default 20 to 16

Dev note: With our changes to body damage multipliers in Update 2.4, the Vetterli Cyclone was able to rapidly and consistently kill players with 2 shots anywhere within its effective range. At 120 damage, the Cyclone’s 2-tap potential is still present, but requires upper body hits to get consistently.

Dev note: This update, we’ve been looking at making some less frequently used weapons feel smoother and more enjoyable to use by tweaking some of their slowest animations.
Flame Rifle
Increased time of a single barrage from around 1.5s to around 2s.
Slightly increased max Oil Ammo to allow for longer barrage
Slightly decreased damage against Targets and Brutes
Fixed an issue that stopped the pumping animation from being interrupted

Dev note: Overall, the Flame Rifle feels like it’s in a good spot—however, with these tweaks, it gets a boost in usability. In practice, the changes to target damage are small, mainly to offset the longer barrage time.
Rebalance of Traits found in the world
Meatheads, Brutes, and Ursa Mortis are now guaranteed to drop Trait Spurs on death.
All non-sealed Trait Spurs found in-world now start fading after first use.
After interacting with a Trait, a 90 second countdown begins, after which the Trait will fade into dust, leaving a scorchmark and bone dust in its place.
Sealed Trait Spurs (those that cost Pledge Marks) will not fade after first use and can be interacted with for the full duration of the mission
Trait Spurs now spawn at a slightly decreased rate in the world randomly (at towers, in compounds, etc.)
The pool of possible Trait Spurs dropped by Meatheads has been expanded, reducing the average Upgrade Point value from dropped Trait Spurs.
Trait Spurs that do spawn in the world are of a higher quality than previously, making finding them more worthwhile
Trait Spurs are now visible and audible in Dark Sight within a short radius.

Dev note: These changes should make Trait Spurs found in the world feel more special to find, while rewarding players that actively Hunt for them with consistent ways to get Traits from large monsters. This change also has an effect on the value of seeking out Wild Targets, giving those who fight them more exclusive rewards compared to those just passing by on their way to the exit at a later point to grab their free Death Cheat.
Increased duration of “The Sun” Tarot Card’s effect to 90 sec from 60 sec.
Dark Sight Decoy dropped from “The Magician” Tarot Card now also triggers the Red Clue effect and Boss Target whispers for enemy teams.
“The World” now rewards 1 Clue reward (Event Points, the Conduit Trait buffs, etc.) per Boss Target discovered with it.
“The Tower” Tarot Card now does additional damage against Boss Targets and kills Wild Targets
Players can now always find Tarot Cards in the world at certain points of interest:
“The Garden and “The Tower” at the Postal Supply
“The Magician” and “The Hanged Man” at the Clockmaker's Supply
“The Moon” and “The Judgement” at the Sealed Hoard
“The Empress” and “The Chariot” at the Burned Convoys
“The Pathfinder” and “The High Priestess” at the Scout Towers.
We’ve expanded the number of entities in-game which change states visibly after being used by players. Enemy teams can use this information to retrace the steps of other Hunters.
The following objects now leave visible traces or remain after player interaction, making it easier to retrace enemy steps and plan ambushes:
Envelopes: Now are more obviously torn open and remain open after interaction.
Explosive/ Oil/ Poison Barrels: Leave broken remains after exploding.
Dogs and Chickens: Their corpses remain in their cages after being killed.
Birds/Ducks: Leave feathers on takeoff and death. Bird and duck corpses also remain when killed.
Traits: Now leave scorch marks on the ground after use, providing a persistent visual indicator.
Doors: Doors are fully closed by default. Once opened, doors never return to their fully closed state, making it easier to track player movement through buildings.
Ammo Packs: Now open and remain open after use.
Breakable Fences: Vaulting over some wooden fences will cause them to crack, leaving visible evidence of traversal.
First Aid Kits & Medical Packs: Using them leaves behind bloody rags on the ground.
Animal Cage Lanterns: Animal cage lanterns now leave broken remains when destroyed by players.
Hunt Dollar and Blood Bond Purses: Interacting with these purses now visually opens them.
Brutes and Ursa Mortis are weaker to Poison Damage.
Meatheads, Immolators, Hellhounds, and Water Devils are slightly weaker to Poison Damage.
Immolators retain their invulnerability to poison clouds.
Immolators now cause little charcoaling damage with their attacks, if not soaked.
Brutes, Ursa Mortis, and Meatheads are slightly more resistant to Arrows and Bolts.
Alive and burning AIs can burn players by contact now. Burning corpses don’t.
The Butcher now reignites the hook fire if extinguished when he frenzies.
Grunts, Armoreds, Meatheads, Brutes, Ursa Mortis, and Bileweavers deal Fire Damage while they die with the fire death animation (not when rag-dolling).
New ambient idle break animations have been added to the monster cast to make them feel more alive.
Hellborn is now more resistant to explosives and weaker to Water Bottles.
Hellborn is now guaranteed to drop either Death Cheat, Relentless, Rampage, or Remedy when killed.

Slightly decreased the volume of some exterior echoes that can be heard when enclosed by rocks or brick walls

Hunters,
Update 2.6.0.1 is now live, below you will find the patch notes.

Please note that we are currently compensating players who purchased content that had its price adjusted in this update. Compensation will be rolled out progressively throughout today, and we expect the process to be completed by the end of the day.
If you do not receive your refund by tomorrow, please contact our Support team.

Hunters, welcome to Post Malone’s Murder Circus Encore! Don't buy a ticket, there's no need in this place. Just watch your back as we cut to the chase!
Check out the Update 2.6 Patch Notes and the Event description below.

No one knows the Murder Circus' dangers better than the former Ringmaster, Post Malone. Now known only as The Disciple of Death, he’s become a deadlier Hunter than ever. If the Murder Circus appears again, he intends to annihilate it. And he isn’t the only one. Former clown Giggles is in mourning for the life she lost when the circus was Corrupted. Mad with grief, she gathers a new group of performer Hunters to fight it. If they destroy the Corrupted circus once and for all, maybe they can start something new.
Ursa Mortis is back and fiercer than ever. Two-headed bear monstrosity with increased health and damage.
Ursa Mortis can now break through the fence of the Circus while chasing players.
Cannot be knocked down by explosives.
Triggers traps with roar attacks.
The Shredder returns as a reworked Scarce Weapon, once again only found at the circus. The changes aim to reduce its overall power and convenience, helping it to better fit into the arsenal.
The bounce adjustment has been removed, meaning that the blades will never try to target players or AI
Instead, the bounce is solely decided based on physics.
The weapon now needs to be manually charged after each shot instead of auto-charging.
This means that the rate of fire has been reduced significantly.
It is no longer auto charged on equip.
The loaded blade will no longer spin forever; instead, it will now spin down after some time, meaning it will need to be recharged to keep it useable.
It can be recharged by pressing the ‘X’ on keyboard or ‘D-pad Up’ on controller.
Unequipping the weapon will no longer stop the blade from spinning, instead it will continue to spin for a set duration while it's on your back.
This means that it can be ready to fire quicker from unequip than the previous version if the user keeps it charged.
The blade projectiles can no longer pierce Hunters and AI.
They will now stick into bodies like Bolts and Arrows.

The Troupes also make a return with the circus, with each Troupe having a unique Trait available to it for a Pledge Mark cost. This time though, players can pledge to as many Troupes as they wish as long as they can pay the relevant Pledge Mark costs. Troupes and their Traits include:
The Knifethrower Troupe- Blademancer (2 PMs): While using Dark Sight, retriable ammo in front of you returns automatically to your inventory. (100m range)
The Mystic Troupe – Communion (1 PM) : While using Dark Sight, temporarily lower your Max HP by 15 to heal your teammate 75 HP and remove their negative status effects. (25m range)
The Trickshooter Troupe - Crack shot (1 PM) : Reduce sway for weapons and increase zoom level in iron sights for rifles and pistols with stocks. Excludes shotguns and sawn-off variants.
The Strongman Troupe – Bruiser (1PM) : Reduces melee stamina consumption and greatly reduces flinching when taking damage.
The Ringmaster Troupe - Corpse Seer (2PMs) : Receive Dark Sight Boost when looting downed Hunters.
Added the new High Striker booth for players to test their strength. Gives a variable number of Event Points depending on melee damage dealt.
The Score is shared over all the High Strikers found in the Mission
With Update 2.6, we’re introducing a new way to customize your profile and display your achievements: Profile Cards.
An avatar, typically showing a Hunter or monster.
Up to 3 badges, showcasing mastery of specific items or in-game progression.
Up to 3 stat trackers, allowing you to display various stats from kills with your favorite items and Hunter, bounty earned, and more. Stats display primarily Bounty Hunt and Bounty Clash statistics.
A title that displays mastery of specific items, nicknames, or achievements.
A cosmetic frame.

Most rewards for Player Profile Cards are earned through progression and gameplay, while some are tied to Events and/or Story Challenges, and some can be purchased. Most stats and progression tied to the Player Cards are starting from scratch, and are not retroactively unlocked, with a few exceptions for stats that tracked before Update 2.6.

These cards appear anywhere you’d previously be able to see players’ profiles and stats—the Death screen, Last Mission screen, by clicking on your teammates in the lobby. Additionally, your team’s cards will be shown during the “Match Found” sequence in the lobby.
Player profiles can be customized through the reworked career tab, alongside Story Challenges.

Story Challenges is a new feature providing players with a completely new way of learning about the game’s lore, the story of its Hunters, and earning valuable rewards. Story Challenges are structured into Chapters which each contain a set of thematical challenges—by completing these, the player will earn valuable rewards and unveil the story one part at a time.
You can find this new feature in the newly updated Challenges screen which now includes both Weekly and Story Challenges. Update 2.6 will feature the two following Story Challenges upon release:

Placed Ping Markers remain for 15 seconds by default. There are a few exceptions to this duration.
Danger Ping Markers remain for 2 seconds
Ping Markers placed on traps remain for 24 seconds
Ping Markers now show up on the compass.
Markers become less opaque when aiming down sights
Overall visibility is improved as environmental light no longer affects a Ping Marker’s color.
All Ping Markers now appear directly on the compass, matching their in-world position and icon.
The compass UI has been redesigned for improved clarity, especially when multiple Markers are active.

Developer Notes: We’re thrilled to introduce our overhauled Ping Marker system. The new system introduces new Marker types, and clearer visibility. Please let us know how the new system feels in action!
The compass has also been reworked to better accommodate icons displayed on the compass. Please share your thoughts on the new compass and any further improvements you’d like to see.
Increased Centennial Wildland spread from 17.5 to 22.5
Added a small random chance to spawn a Locked Weapon Box containing the Wildland and Homestead in Watchtowers. This can be unlocked for 3 Pledge Marks.
New Status Effect: Wet state. Hunters are considered Wet when traversing deep water, and for 15 seconds afterwards. While in the Wet state, Hunters:
Do not burn or catch fire as easily
Recover charcoaled health faster
Have wet footstep audio/are louder and easier to track
Recovery Shots and the Relentless Trait now restore Health Chunks with 24 points of charcoaling.
Added hints that display when interacting with all Traits and Event-exclusive weapons, describing their use and effects.
Burn Traits can no longer be stacked, meaning Hunters can only have one instance of Relentless, Remedy, and Rampage instead of 3.
Beetle cocoon spawns can now provide any Beetle type.
New Item that can be found randomly.
Can be thrown, creating a large splash of water on impact.
Applies new “Wet” Status Effect to Hunters and Immolators.
Puts out most fires and burning Hunters.
Oil fires are excluded from this. Throwing Water Bottles on oil fires will instead create a large burst of flames.
Can be shot while on the ground to make it explode.
Cannot be stored, and breaks if dropped.
Added Immolator Wet Status Effect
Immolators enter the Wet state when walking in deep waters, under heavy rain, or when splashed with the Water Bottle. They die with a direct Water Bottle hit.
Immolators in the Wet state can’t ignite, are slower and weaker (receive more damage).
The Hive’s speed has been slowed when in water.
The Assassin’s health has been reduced to align its time to kill with other Boss Targets.
Slightly increased the volume of the Maynard Silencer without Subsonic Ammo at long distances
Decreased the audio occlusion for some environmental rocks that are common in Mammon’s Gulch

Slightly increased the stereo width of gun tails to make gunshots sound more immersive. Note that this change only affects the late echoes and reverberation of the gunshot sounds, so you can still tell the direction of gunshots as well as before.
Adjusted shotgun interior tail sounds to be more readable and in-line with rifle and pistol gunshot interior tails
Slightly Decreased volume of shovel and spear flyby sounds
Rich Presence for Hunt
Rich presence text is now available in Steam and Discord for users who opt into the feature.
Players are displayed as parties, and rich presence gives information as to their current game status in the lobby or in a specific game mode.
Updated icons for weak Shots to better distinguish them from standard Shots.
Reduced PvE pressure
Monsters are introduced gradually; new players face a limited variety in early Missions, and all monsters appear after reaching Bloodline Rank 20.
Bots scalable difficulty
To ease the onboarding for new players, we introduced 2 new presets of difficulty for the Hunter Bots.
As long as players level up, they will face more difficult Hunter Bots. Hunter Bots still last until Bloodline Rank 10.

items.text: Hunters,
The live servers are up again. You will find the list of fixes below.
Happy hunting!
Fixed the mouse cursor being displayed after loading into a Mission
Fixed the incorrect display of Locked Extraction Points on the map and compass
Fixed the post-Mission summary screen from appearing every time when coming back to the lobby from other screens
Hunters,
Update 2.5 and the new Live Event, Web of the Empress, are here!

Face the terrifying Bileweavers, Corrupted creatures swarming the bayou with their nests in the brand-new 17th Compound. To aid your hunt, harness the power of Tarot Cards, a new Consumable that grants unique effects to twist the tide of battle.
Alongside the Event, Update 2.5 delivers numerous changes and a host of fixes to sharpen your hunt.
Step inside the Web of the Empress...if you dare!

The Corruption has birthed new monsters: The Bileweavers, spider-like beings who hatch from eggs with venom ready in their fangs. While an individual Bileweaver is weak, they like to swarm together to overwhelm intruders. They're bent on defending their territory—not just their own massive nests, but also the small web-covered areas throughout the Incursion zones.
The Bileweaver is a new spider-like monster.
Individually, the Bileweaver is very weak, but they attack in groups, acting like a swarm.
Bileweavers are area defenders and can be found in the Bileweaver Nest and in small groups in other little web-covered locations.
The Bileweavers have created massive, web-covered nests. Hunters brave enough to enter and skilled enough to leave alive will find treasure hidden within.
Bileweaver nests contain:
Exclusive Scarce Weapons
3 Tarot Cards
Destiny’s Dial: A machine that gives randomized rewards (Traits, buffs, and more)
Scarce and Burn Traits
Restoration Kit
Ammo Resupply Box
4-Shot Boon, XP and Dark Sight Boost envelopes
A lootable hunter's corpse.

Get ready to experience the tools of The Witch, the journey of The Fool, and the power of The Empress. This update, we've introduced 12 Tarot Cards: single-use Consumables, each with a unique ability based on their traditional meaning. Use a card to gain its power...and sometimes, pay its price. It may be enough to tip the scales of fate.
The unique effect of each card is below:
The World: Reveals all Boss Targets.
The Moon: Grants 2 seconds of Dark Sight Boost
The Garden: Fully heals and removes Bleeding, Burning, and Poison for you and your teammates.
The Fool: Copies the last Tarot Card you used this Mission.
The Tower: Kills Monsters and damages Targets within a 65m radius. Your Hunter catches on fire.

The Magician: Places a Dark Sight Decoy at your location causes Heavy Bleeding on use.: Dev Note: The Dark Sight Decoy looks like an enemy Hunter to other players observing it with Dark Sight Boost. The Decoy also triggers Instinct on enemy Hunters. The Decoy has a distinct audio effect and can be dispelled by interacting with it physically. Decoys dropped by you or your own team do not show up in Dark Sight Boost or trigger Instinct for you or your team.
The Devil: Reduces the sway and spread (excluding shotguns) for weapons until your Hunter is downed, then destroys an additional Health Chunk.
The Sun: Grants an increased Regeneration buff for 60 seconds.
Judgement: Doubles time of all current buffs. Reduces your Hunter’s HP to 1.
The Hanged Man: Allows you to spectate the nearest enemy Hunter for a limited time. The spectated Hunter hears a warning afterwards.

The Empress: Grants the Catalyst Trait, the Necromancer Trait, and one random Burn or Scarce Trait.: Dev Note: Traits are added in the order mentioned above and cannot exceed the Hunter’s maximum number of Traits. The Catalyst Trait can only be obtained via the Tarot Card “The Empress” or as a random reward from Destiny’s Dial.

The Chariot: Swaps Locked and Unlocked Extraction Points for all teams (only in Bounty Hunt). Destroys 1 Health Chunk. This ability has a five-minute global cooldown and can’t be used during the last five minutes of the Mission.

Dev Note: Since there are quite a few new effects and abilities to learn, we have added a small quality of life feature for the Tarot Cards, where if you inspect them when equipped, a small hint pop-up will appear on the top right of the screen detailing the equipped Tarot Card’s effect. This feature can also be turned off via a setting in the menu.
Tarot Cards can be acquired by:
Finding them in the world: 3 Tarot Cards are available in each Bileweaver Nest, and some have a chance to spawn at web-covered locations around the map.
Collecting Dark Tribute rewards: 2 Tarot Cards are earned at the first Dark Tribute stage, with 1 Tarot Card earned at each subsequent stage.
Looting them from dead Hunters: Any Tarot Cards carried by dead Hunters can be stolen when looting, so long as you have a free Consumable slot for them.

notes.title: Locked Extraction Points & Central Extraction Points

items.text: With Web of the Empress, we’re introducing an additional Extraction Point to the center of the map. This Extract Point is always locked by default, and must be unlocked with the Tarot Card “The Chariot” to become accessible. These Extracts can be convenient and allow for speedy getaways, but are in exposed locations. One other random Extraction Point is locked at game start.

The Tarot Card “The Chariot” swaps which Extraction Points are locked and unlocked. When used by a player, there will be a global cooldown on the card for five minutes. Players can still consume the card to make space in their inventory, but no extracts can be swapped while this cooldown is active. Players will receive a small status effect icon with a timer to denote the cooldown.

We are excited to welcome new Hunters on board in their languages!

Added two new weapons only available in-Mission: the Winfield Wildland and the Caldwell Homestead 78. These weapons cannot be purchased for Hunt Dollars and may only be found in the Bileweaver Nests in Bounty Hunt.
Homestead 78: a long-barrelled cousin of the Rival 78, this shotgun packs extra punch at medium range. Comparable to a double-barrel Romero 77.
Wildland: this modified Centennial is a specialized hunting rifle that does increased damage, with a longer barrel and improved magazine capacity. In addition, it sports a swift reload mechanism.
Each Scarce Weapon belongs to separate weapon families than the base Rival and Centennial.
Added new options for choosing how a Hunter selects equipment that they pick up.
Weapons: when enabled, picked up Weapons will automatically be selected.
Tools: when enabled, picked up Tools will automatically be selected. Also applies to thrown melee Tools and traps.
Consumables: when enabled, picked up Consumables will automatically be selected.
Equipment gained from looting Tool Boxes, Hunters, Beetles, etc. will not be affected by these settings and will never be auto-selected.

By default, all of these new settings are turned on. However, they can be adjusted based on preference, meaning the previous selected behaviors from before these changes are still possible if you are not comfortable with the changes.
Melee-focused weapons, Tools, and variants with melee attachments have had their maximum reach slightly increased.
The hit detection method has also been improved, meaning that horizontal melee attacks will now hit more consistently.

Previously, the detection method was akin to a thin line which followed the animation in order to detect a hit. This has now been improved to include some ‘thickness,’ meaning the detection better matches the weapon’s size.
These changes focus on melee attacks swipes, and for the most part does not affect stabs, buttstock hits or pistol whips etc.
Affected Weapons
All melee Tools (includes Throwing Knives, etc.)
All dedicated melee weapons
Certain variants with melee attachments (Riposte, Claw, etc.)

With the changes to body damage multipliers, we revisited this change as it seems necessary to slow the reload down again.

All in-world weapons consistently kill Hunters who are hit
Sledgehammers and Wood Axes will kill Armoreds and Immolators in one hit
Pitchforks will kill Armoreds in one throw, while needing two hits for Immolators

Note: This does not apply to Lanterns that are being carried.

Note: Stalker beetle and fire beetle are no longer obtainable from in-world beetle cocoons.

Developer Note: We are experimenting with this based on player feedback, but might revert this change in the next update again based on reception. It is important that players can always reliably find Choke Beetles, which work great for scouting and extinguishing downed team-mates, but if players want to use Beetles with offensive capabilities, we expect them to bring those into the mission.
New deployable found only in-Mission
Can be picked up and deployed on the ground
Acts like a smaller red barrel: damage will start a fuse, detonating it after a few seconds. Fire-based damage will instantly detonate Powder Kegs.

Added Chinese audio localization
Slightly increased the volume of all 3D audio when using a 3rd party 3D audio solution such as Dolby Atmos, Windows Sonic, DTS or Tempest.

Dev Note: We noticed that audio readability was slightly less reliable when using 3rd party 3D audio solutions. After extensive measurements and testing, we found that all 3D sounds were a bit too quiet when compared to CrySptatial—we made some minor adjustments to compensate for this to unify the mix of the game for all 3D audio solutions.

Note that this change does not affect the sound of the game when using CrySpatial or when 3D audio is disabled. A reminder that Hunt: Showdown 1896 is mainly mixed for use with CrySpatial—we recommend turning it on with no other enhancements or 3D audio solutions enabled.
Made the volume of Hunter footstep sounds across all surface types slightly more consistent

Dev Note: We noticed that some of you struggle to accurately judge distances using audio. After an extensive investigation, we found that the volume of Hunter footsteps can vary quite a bit depending on the surface type a Hunter is walking on. We have improved the consistency of footstep volume across similar surface types.

This means that footsteps on metal roofs are still a lot louder than footsteps on other surface types. However, footsteps on coal, for example, will now be more consistent with footsteps on gravel. Running on wood will still be louder than running on fabric, but running on hollow wood is now closer in volume to running on solid wood. Most notably we increased the volume of sneak footsteps on some outlying surface types such as gravel and leaves. You will still be able to ambush other players, but you also get a fair chance to notice them when they ambush you—keep those ears open.

The change is pretty subtle and may be difficult to notice consciously, but we feel it has improved intuitive distance readability quite a bit. You would be surprised by the subtleties your ears will pick up!
Added a specific sweetener sound when firing a shotgun with Slug ammunition
Enhanced the gunshot sound of the New Army to feel a bit more powerful and satisfying
Hunter footsteps and Fusees are now better audible while other loud sounds are playing
Dev Note: We’ve streamlined the Lobby experience and removed the old home screen—the Lobby is now your new home base.
All game modes are accessible from a single Lobby screen.
Switch between modes (Shooting Range, Bounty Clash, Bounty Hunt) using arrows or by selecting the game mode tile.
No need to reform parties when changing modes (for invited squads only).
Parties with random players cannot change game modes, since randoms queue for a specific mode.
Progression screens are now under a new Career tab in the main navigation.
Last Mission Stats and Team Details are viewable directly in the Lobby.
The Newsfeed has been relocated to the top-right corner.
Dev Note: In a long-requested feature, duos can now search for a random third teammate in trios.
In a duo party, set “Your Team” to Trios.
The matchmaking button will change to Find Teammate.
Solo players will now be matched with other solos or with a duo.
Dev Note: We’ve made equipping and managing loadouts smoother.
Traits are now embedded in the Gear screen—see your full loadout while selecting Traits.
Added shortcut to Clear All Traits (with confirmation pop-up).
Double-click always equips weapons (no longer opens Item Details).
Exiting weapon comparisons now only requires one Esc press.
Dev Note: Based on your feedback, we’ve simplified cosmetic tiers.
All cosmetics are now either Legendary or Mythic.
Mythic items (orange background) are Event exclusives, with tags showing the Event they came from.
Common/Uncommon/Rare tags have been removed.
Sorting by rarity has been removed from filters.
Dev Note: Bundle purchases are clearer and more transparent.
Individual cosmetics in a bundle are now clearly marked.
On purchase, you can choose to buy a single item or the full bundle.
The bundle preview shows all included items.
Only the bundle price is displayed to avoid confusion with individual pricing.
Dev Note: We’ve refreshed the UI to better match the game’s art style.
Most UI components, buttons, and backgrounds have a new look.
Recruitment buttons on the Active Roster screen now have unique artwork.
Dev Note: You no longer need to hunt down unlocked rewards.
Cosmetics and Hunters unlocked in the Battle Pass can now be applied or recruited directly from the Battle Pass progression screen.
Navmesh regeneration has been improved to guarantee correct navmesh on Missions with location variations (e.g. Bileweaver Nests).

notes.title: Improved Butcher and Scrapbeak Boss Target Reachability

items.text: The Butcher and Scrapbeak can now reach and attack Hunters in most places where they were unexpectedly unreachable before.
Melee attacks have animation variations that are used on some of the new reached locations, depending on the attacker and target’s relative positions and surroundings. Attack damage remains the same.
Bots shoot more at monsters, giving away their position to players.
Bots are more effective at dealing with monsters, specifically Armored, Concertina Armored, and Water Devils.
Increased bot firing rates during player encounters. Despite shooting more often, their low accuracy keeps overall lethality unchanged.
Improved the bots’ behavior when in close range to use melee attacks more often.
Reduced head multiplier damage for Armored and Concertina Armored NPCs
Added an idle behavior to Brute where it sometimes stops, bothered by some swarms insects while wandering around.
The trait pool for drops from Meathead and Brute has been rebalanced. All traits have the same weight now, except for Scarce and Burn traits.
Grunts have received a full rework that improves their stability and scalability. Some of the most noticeable improvements are:
Better spawning: Popping Grunts are less likely to happen, and strange animation transitions on spawning have been fixed.
Grunts move towards Hunters when they are shot and the hit impact is heard, despite shot origin sound taking priority if heard.
Grunts move slower in water.
Distractors (e.g. bell) now don’t fully take all attention; Grunts prioritize Hunters if they are in sight.
Grunt pathfinding has been refined to improve navigation. In certain scenarios, this makes Grunts take more direct routes toward players, reducing swarming behavior.

With Judgement of the Fool, we are updating our approach to Weekly Challenge and Event pacing. Individual Weekly Challenge Event Point rewards are reduced to between 500-1000 EPs per challenge. However, with the Event itself being significantly longer, players will be able to earn more Event Points overall, and at their own pace. Weekly Challenge sets now only feature 5 challenges rather than 6, making all weekly sets easier to complete.

Although the total number of challenges per week may have decreased, we have subsequently increased the reward for one challenge per week from 10 Blood Bonds to 20, so the total awarded through weekly challenges remains unchanged compared to previous events – 50 BBs per week.
Hunter
Hunter body part damage multipliers have been changed to these values:
Upper Torso: 1.3 (same as before)
Torso: 1.2 (previously 1)
Arms: 0.9 (previously 0.8)
Legs: 0.8 (previously 0.7)
These changes mean that at all ranges, damage to less critical body parts now have a greater effect in firefights.
Damage drop-off plateaus:
All Compact Ammo weapons start losing damage at 20m
All Medium Ammo weapons start losing damage at 30m
All Long Ammo weapons start losing damage at 40m
Upper-Torso:
Any rifle deals at least 50 damage
Compact Ammo pistols deal at least 25 damage but less than 50 damage
Any Medium or Long Ammo pistol deals at least 50 damage
Torso:
Any rifle deals at least 50 damage at any distance, with the exception of the Officer Carbine
Any pistol deals at least 25 damage, with some powerful pistols being able to deal 50 damage
Limbs:
All rifles and pistols deal at least 25 damage to arms or legs at all distances
Exceptions to this ruleset are the Bornheim family and Nagant Silencer, due to their low base damage.
FMJ:
FMJ still extends the damage drop start by 10m
FMJ has a slightly higher end damage value, making the ammo slightly stronger at distances
Spitzer:
Spitzer has a higher end damage value, retaining the base damage better, but due to the lower base damage still dealing less damage overall

The above mentioned drop-off rules are without any penetration involved; with penetration, the thresholds might not be met. Due to their reduced base damage, some silencers might be exceptions to the drop-off ruleset. The Dolch 96 sits between compact and medium projectiles, with the weapon having characteristics—like muzzle velocity and damage—of a Medium Ammo pistol, but following the rules set for Compact Ammo pistols more. The Quad Derringer, which is not mentioned specifically here, performs similarly to the Bornheim No.3.
Silencer Balance Changes
The silencer damage reduction rule has been adjusted to reduce the effect on Compact and Medium Ammo.
Compact and Medium Ammo reduction goes from 10% to 5%.
Long Ammo reduction stays at 10%.

While downed, there are now two speeds at which a Hunter’s body can burn: Fast and Slow.
Fast

notes.title: A downed body will be considered as Fast burning if

items.text: It is inside a fire volume (Lantern, Fire Bomb, oil patch, etc.).
It is ignited from any source of fire. After five seconds, it will fizzle down to Slow burning.
If reignited again, the body will Fast burn for another 5 seconds.
Fast burning is similar to the burning speed prior to what was experienced before this update.
Slow

notes.title: A downed body will be considered as Slow burning if

items.text: It is not in a fire volume, or the 5 seconds of Fast burning upon ignition have passed.
Slow burning is 45% slower compared to what was experienced before this update.
Submerged Bodies
Hunter bodies that are underwater can now be burned by fire volumes at a very slow speed.

With past changes, the cost of burning a body has become low, with Hunters often having a Tool or other weapon they can use to ignite a Hunter quickly (and sometimes at quite some range). With these changes, we aim to reduce some convivence from the Tool/weapon layer and instead bring more relevance to world items like Lanterns or Consumables such as the Fire Bomb.

Dev Note: Along with the launch of Hunt: Showdown 1896, we added various location-based ambient sounds to the world of Hunt. The original intent for these sounds to be part of the game was to increase the players’ immersion by further connecting visuals and audio. While we feel that these sounds fulfill their intended purpose, we received feedback from the community and within the team that, in some scenarios, these sounds can mask important gameplay feedback. With Update 2.4 we have implemented a range of mixing improvements to our ambient sounds, improving overall mix clarity and readability. The positioned ambient sounds (random wood creaks, etc.) are drastically reduced in volume and limited in their frequency of use to blend with the global ambience more seamlessly. Location-based ambience loops (e.g. forest ambiences) have been tweaked in their frequency content to leave more “space” for important gameplay information.
Thanks to everyone in the community who provided feedback on this!
Improved audio readability of vertical Hunter footsteps inside buildings:
Reworked and increased the upstairs wood footstep sound layer and added a unique downstairs wood footstep sound layer
Added upstairs and downstairs footstep sound layers for other surface types including rock, hollow metal and fabric
Upstairs and downstairs footstep layers can now be heard from outside buildings, allowing you to more clearly determine the position of enemy Hunters when approaching buildings

Dev Note: These improvements aim to instantly give you information about the position of an enemy Hunter without having to solely rely on psychoacoustic localization cues. To do so, we are adding and increasing layers to footsteps that only trigger when a Hunter is above or below you within a building. Footsteps above you now sound a bit more direct and bassy, while footsteps below you sound sharper and more hollow. We would love your feedback on these changes.

releases.displayName: Developer Insight - Fair Play Task Force Update

items.text: Hunters,

As part of our commitment to keeping you informed about our Fair Play Task Force and our actions against cheaters we would like to share with you an update. Since January we have banned a total of 4929 cheaters. In this blog you’ll find a breakdown of these bans by MMR levels along with some insights into how we categorize different cheaters.
Banned Players by MMR distribution

The chart above shows the distribution of MMR levels among players who were banned in recent months. As indicated, cheaters are significantly more likely to be found at higher MMR levels, as their performance improves drastically once they gain the advantage of cheating software. However, bans also occur at lower MMR levels. This can be attributed to players intentionally dying to maintain a low MMR, or more commonly, players being banned when they launch the game with cheats for the first time—before they had the opportunity to use them in a match, or shortly after starting to. We have methods in place to detect when a banned player creates a new account and continues cheating. In such cases, we enforce a zero-tolerance policy: repeat offenders are instantly banned upon account creation.
Types of cheaters
In general, we tend to see two main types of cheaters: “rage cheaters” and “togglers.”

Rage cheaters are the most obvious group. They typically use blatant cheating methods and make little to no effort to hide their behavior. Their goal is often to disrupt the game as much as possible before getting banned, using less sophisticated tools or behaving in ways that are easy to detect. As a result, they are usually caught and banned very quickly.

Togglers, on the other hand, use more subtle and sophisticated methods. They don’t cheat throughout the entire match—instead, they enable cheats only during specific moments where it can provide a critical advantage. From our perspective, these players often appear to be playing normally most of the time, but in certain situations, their performance improves in an unnatural and statistically abnormal way. Because of this selective behavior, our systems need to collect more data over a longer period before it can confirm a ban. This is why some bans take longer and why togglers are often found in higher MMR brackets.

There are also cases where rage cheaters climb the MMR ladder rapidly due to the extreme advantage provided by their cheats. In such instances, they may end up getting banned when they reach higher skill brackets.

One common toggler tactic involves only one player in a group actively using cheats, while sharing information—such as enemy positions—with their teammates through voice chat. This makes detection more challenging, as it’s difficult to determine who is actually cheating and who is simply receiving relayed information. We take extra care in these situations to avoid banning innocent players who may be unaware of their teammates’ actions.

We are actively developing advanced systems focused on identifying and banning cheaters at higher MMR levels. These tools are designed to distinguish genuinely skilled players from those using subtle forms of cheating. While we cannot share specific details about how these systems work—for security reasons—we want to emphasize that this is a top priority for us.
How To Report Suspected Cheaters
If you encounter someone who you think is cheating, who was not picked up by the automatic ban system then please follow the below steps:

While on the death screen you can click “Show killer profile” or press “R” (for PC), RT (for Xbox)/R2 (for PS5) and then select “Report”. You can then fill in the reasons and add any additional information.

Another way to report people is after the Mission is over you can go onto the “Last Mission – Team Details” menu and click on the profile you would like to report and then click on “Actions Menu” or press “F” (PC)/ press X (Xbox)/ press square (PS5) and then “Report”.

Additionally, you can report via our website if you have any additional context you would like to share. You can do this by going to www.huntshowdown.com. In the bottom right corner of the screen, you'll see "Please log in for support". After logging in, open a new ticket, select your language and platform as well as "I'd like to report another player" and the bot will guide you through the process.

We hope this sheds light on what we are doing to combat cheaters; we can’t give away all our methods, but we endeavor to give you as much transparent information as possible! Watch this space for more updates as the year unfolds.

Hunters,
Update 2.3 and the Garden of the Witch event are now live! Below, you'll find all the details about the latest update and the event.
Happy hunting!

Cursed nature and corrupted metal clash as new Hunters join the fray. The Bruja duo have seen their healing plants cursed and their cures fail as Corruption has poisoned the very soil. The Welders feel their minds altered and bent by the blood-soaked metal brought their way. Each fights the Corruption with their own strengths: the Brujas with organic mysticism, the Welders with industrial occult practices and fire.

Garden of the Witch introduces Event-exclusive Traits. These are selected from past Events and are only available by spending Pledge Marks in-Mission for the duration of the Event and will be removed once Garden of the Witch concludes. They have a chance of spawning where other Sealed Traits can spawn, and there will always be one that spawns randomly at the Rare Supply.
Event-exclusive Scarce Traits: Blademancer, Corpse Seer, Gunrunner

Rewards that appeared in past Events at the Sealed Hoard are now on the move at a new type of Supply Point called the Rare Supply. These rewards appear together at various locations and are marked by black canvas and with a unique map icon. There is always one Rare Supply per Mission.
The following Sealed Items are guaranteed at the Rare Supply:
Sealed Bounty Token (with a chance)
Master Clue
Full Restoration Kit
1 Random Event-exclusive Sealed Scarce Trait
Additionally, the Rare Supply will also always feature the following Sealed rewards, all of which can also be found randomly across Supply Points, arsenals, and watch towers in the world:
Four Shot Boon
Experience Boon
Dark Sight Boon
Sealed Cash Register
Sealed Ammo and Tools

1 PM per 25 Event Points collected
2 PMs for Banishing the Boss Target in Bounty Clash
3 PMs for becoming the Soul Survivor

When looting a Hunter, you steal their Pledge Marks up to a maximum of 6 total. The looted Hunter loses any Pledge Marks stolen, but can retain some if the looting Hunter reaches their maximum amount (6 PMs) in the process.

Back in October, we shared details of upcoming hit validation and trade window improvements that went live with Update 2.2. Since the changes have been allowed to play out in a live environment, we wanted to circle back with an overview of the results and improvements observed so far.

To recap, we adjusted the specific time limit for how long a player can still shoot or land a hit after death from 800 to 75 milliseconds. Our goal was to fine tune the system to create a fairer and more consistent ecosystem for everyone, prioritizing player reaction times over external factors like connection speed.

notes.title: Kill Trades VS Total Player Kills

items.text: One of the key metrics we’ve been closely monitoring since rolling out the trade window adjustment is the percentage of kills that qualify as "Trade." A kill trade specifically occurs when two players eliminate each other within a specified window. This definition encompasses a variety of scenarios, from intentional gameplay mechanics like bleeding out or being taken down by a well-timed throwable, to the "bad trades" that have been a source of community concern.

Our data shows a clear and sustained decline in the percentage of kill trades since the update went live. In fact, the figure has effectively been halved compared to pre-update levels. This is a substantial improvement and highlights the tangible impact of the recent changes on gameplay dynamics.
(Please note the large spike on December 12th is due to restricted data during server downtime as Update 2.2 was rolled out)

We also analyzed the percentage of hit invalidations with our 2.2 adjustments, which refers to the instances where a shot does not register as intended, which can significantly affect combat, outcomes, and player satisfaction. The goal with this change was to prevent hit validation from attacks made by players who were already marked as downed on the server.
As anticipated, we have been able to track a significant rise in the number of invalidated attacks following the update.

To better understand the context behind this, we went on to analyze the root causes of invalidations, both before and after the update. Before changes went live with 2.2, most invalidated hits stemmed from general timeouts. This meant a damage request took too long to reach the server, usually due to connectivity issues between the player and the server.

Following the update, we can see the landscape has changed significantly. The leading cause of invalidations is now projectile launch prevention. This occurs when a shot is rejected at the moment of launch because the shooter was already downed and beyond the 75 millisecond death threshold.
By addressing community feedback and fine-tuning the mechanics contributing to unfair kill trades, we’ve made measurable progress in creating a more balanced and satisfying experience.
We are always working to refine gameplay in Hunt, and we will continue to share updates and insights as we do. As always, we thank you for your feedback, and happy hunting!
Hunters,

~ The Hunt Team
